_meta.title: Beverly FY2026-2030 Financial Forecast, general fund operating budget
_meta.source: City of Beverly Financial Forecast FY2026 to FY2030, Financial Forecast Committee, December 2025
_meta.notes: General fund operating budget only; enterprise funds excluded. Committee uses a deliberately conservative revenue method and objective expenditure method, so actual deficits may run slightly smaller than the pre-balancing figures shown. The Mayor's submitted budget is balanced by law; these are the pre-balancing projections that show the structural gap. The retirement line here (14.98M FY27) is the forecast's own figure and runs slightly below the PERAC schedule (15.58M FY27) in pension.json; treat pension.json as the authoritative pension source and this as the forecast's internal assumption.

summary.note: Pre-balancing. Revenue grows ~2.9%/yr, expenditures ~5%/yr; the gap compounds.

growthAssumptions.note: The forecast's own per-line assumptions. These are the inputs to reuse in the bridge model.

lines.schoolFunding: 3%/yr plus stepped enrollment to 60 slots per grade

reserves.note: Reserves healthy now but drawing down. ~$7M spent from reserves before FY26 close (City Hall, roads, stabilization, OPEB transfer). DLS free-cash policy target is 3-8% of the general fund.

riskFlags.federalSchoolGrants: BPS relies on ~$2.5M/yr in federal grants the committee says the city could not replace if cut.
riskFlags.structuralNote: The committee calls this deficit 'qualitatively different' from prior years; the strategies used to close past gaps (roads shift to free cash $2.7M, excess levy capacity $1.4M, Rx restructuring) 'no longer exist'.
